title: Risk prediction in IgA nephropathy: from conventional models to machine learning, deep learning, and precision nephrology

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Risk prediction in IgA nephropathy: from conventional models to machine learning, deep learning, and precision nephrology》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Since its first description by Jean Berger and Nicole Hinglais in 1968 [1], IgA nephropathy (IgAN) has been recognized as the most common primary glomerular disease worldwide [2]. Its diagnosis relies on renal biopsy, which typically shows predominant or co-dominant IgA-containing immune complex deposits in the glomerular mesangium, with or without accompanying IgG or IgM deposits on immunofluorescence [3]. As a leading cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) [4], IgAN exhibits notable geographic variation in epidemiology. It is particularly prevalent in East Asian populations, accounting for 25–50% of primary glomerular diseases, while in Europe and North America, it accounts for about 15–30% [5]. The estimated global incidence is ∼2.5 cases per 100,000 people [6].

【Introduction · S0001-p2】For clinicians, accurately evaluating the long-term risk of IgAN progression remains a significant challenge [7]. The disease course covers a broad range, from patients with persistent microscopic hematuria and minimal proteinuria who stay stable for decades, to those presenting with nephrotic syndrome or rapidly progressing glomerulonephritis who advance to ESKD despite standard treatment [8]. Even among patients with seemingly similar clinical and pathological features, outcomes can vary greatly [9]. Approximately half of patients develop ESKD within 20 years [10], significantly impacting their quality of life and increasing healthcare costs. This prognostic uncertainty makes patient counseling, risk–benefit analysis, and treatment decisions more challenging, often leaving clinicians uncertain about when to intensify monitoring, initiate immunosuppression, or consider enrolling patients in clinical trials.

sections.text:

【Introduction · S0001-p3】In this context, reliable prognostic prediction tools are critically needed to enable early identification of high-risk patients, guide personalized treatment plans, and optimize healthcare resource allocation. Over the past decades, the field has experienced a surge in prognostic modeling studies [11], driven by the increasing availability and integration of diverse data types, including clinical variables, histopathological features, and high-dimensional multi-omics profiles, as well as advances in modeling methodologies ranging from traditional statistical approaches to modern machine learning and deep learning techniques. Given the rapid pace and broad scope of these developments, a timely and comprehensive review is crucial to chart the evolution of models, identify emerging trends, and assess their potential for real-world clinical applications.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Risk prediction in IgA nephropathy: from conventional models to machine learning, deep learning, and precision nephrology》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Pathology-based prediction models · S0003-S2002-p1】The development of pathology-based prediction models has progressively improved clinicians’ ability to assess patient risk and tailor treatment plans. Early research mostly focused on how different pathological classifications could predict outcomes. Yagame et al. [30] conducted a single-center study in Japan using a four-grade pathological classification system; over 15 years of follow-up, they found that patients with grade 4 severe lesions had a renal survival rate of only 22%, providing strong evidence for the predictive role of pathological damage in prognosis. Later, Radford et al. [46] carried out systematic, semi-quantitative evaluations of glomerular pathological changes in a U.S. patient group and proposed a ‘total glomerular score’ that combined four pathological features: glomerulosclerosis, capillary loop damage, cellular crescents, and fibrous adhesions. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that patients with scores above 5 had a significantly higher risk of ESKD, establishing clear therapeutic thresholds for clinical practice.

【Pathology-based prediction models · S0003-S2002-p2】As the significance of pathological information in prognostic modeling became more evident, the traditional Lee classification system, with its complex five-grade structure, limited widespread clinical use. To address this issue, Manno et al. [47] conducted a single-center study in Italy and created a simplified three-tier histological grading system (mild, moderate, severe), demonstrating its better prognostic discrimination compared to the Lee classification. This development highlighted the need for effective prognostic tools to strike a balance between scientific accuracy and practicality in busy clinical settings.

[46] carried out systematic, semi-quantitative evaluations of glomerular pathological changes in a U.S. patient group and proposed a ‘total glomerular score’ that combined four pathological features: glomerulosclerosis, capillary loop damage, cellular crescents, and fibrous adhesions. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that patients with scores above 5 had a significantly higher risk of ESKD, establishing clear therapeutic thresholds for clinical practice.

As the significance of pathological information in prognostic modeling became more evident, the traditional Lee classification system, with its complex five-grade structure, limited widespread clinical use. To address this issue, Manno et al. [47] conducted a single-center study in Italy and created a simplified three-tier histological grading system (mild, moderate, severe), demonstrating its better prognostic discrimination compared to the Lee classification. This development highlighted the need for effective prognostic tools to strike a balance between scientific accuracy and practicality in busy clinical settings.
